Data and methods

Records: 33,000 synthetic demonstration incidents (2015–2025) and 56 Uganda Police Force facilities placed at approximate locality positions. Neither file is an official police record, and facility positions need site verification.

Coordinates

All distances, buffers and densities are computed in Arc 1960 / UTM Zone 36N (EPSG:21096) metres. The WGS84 reference coordinates are used only for display on the web map.

Hotspot index

Incidents reported in the 24 months up to the end of the selected period are binned on a 250 m grid, weighted by recency (6-month half-life), and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel. Density is scaled 0–1, then multiplied by (1 − w) + w × D, where D is distance to the nearest police facility divided by 5 km (capped at 1). Live simulated alerts join the surface as they arrive. Density shows concentration, not statistical significance.

Forecasts

Observed trend: a quasi-Poisson log-linear model of annual counts per crime type (and per division), fitted on 2015–2025 and tested by training on 2015–2022 and predicting 2023–2025. A trend is only carried forward when its slope is significant at 95%; otherwise the projection holds the 2015–2025 mean. Population growth: the 2021–2025 average annual count per district grows with the annual population growth rates you enter, assuming a constant per-capita rate. The band shows ±1 percentage point of growth plus Poisson variation. Predicted hotspot surfaces re-weight 2023–2025 incidents by each division's projected multiplier.

Limits

Reported incidents are not all incidents. There is no time-of-day field, so time patterns use month and day of week. This is an academic decision-support prototype, not a tool for patrol routing, deployment or individual targeting.
